title: Zenobia - discovery: migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery for migrating Zenobia's production assistant from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Discussion covered current architecture, performance pain points (latency and token cost), compatibility concerns with vLLM/TGI, eval parity, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and next steps for a benchmark PoC and pricing. Customer is interested in a 2-4 week pilot with Dedicated capacity and wants to validate latency and eval parity with their prompt set.
next_steps: Jordan to send Dedicated pricing and SKU options (by 2026-03-06)
Priya to draft benchmark plan and required artifacts for 24-72h run (by 2026-03-06)
Zenobia to share sample prompt set, recent usage stats, and a list of highest-volume routes (by 2026-03-05)
Schedule technical PoC kickoff (2-hour session) for next week once pricing agreed
action_items: Jordan Lee: send pricing + Dedicated config options (due 2026-03-06)
Priya Patel: prepare benchmark plan (vLLM/TGI parity checks, latency p95/p99) and infra checklist (due 2026-03-06)
Aisha Khan: provide sample prompt set, current token mix, and top 5 failing prompts (due 2026-03-05)
Liam O'Neil: confirm compliance needs (SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC peering) and on-prem constraints (due 2026-03-08)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Carlos (Zenobia CTO), Aisha (ML Eng), Liam (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Samir. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Carlos: Good, thanks. Appreciate you taking the time. We're looking to move off OpenAI for our customer-facing assistant and wanted to understand Dedicated options.
[00:18] Jordan: Totally — high level do you want hosted or dedicated or are you evaluating both?
[00:22] Carlos: We started on hosted OpenAI, but costs and occasional rate limits are killing our economics. We're leaning Dedicated, maybe Private later for compliance.
[00:30] Priya: Got it. Can you share current usage patterns — tokens per month, p95 latency targets, and models you're using?
[00:36] Aisha: Sure. We're on GPT-4 style endpoints through OpenAI-ish — about 1.8B tokens/month, peak 120 rps, average latency tolerance ~300ms for short prompts, but p95 under 700ms ideally. We also run embeddings for search, about 200k embeddings/day.
[00:52] Samir: And what infra are you running for any self-hosted or TGI/vLLM experiments?
[00:56] Carlos: We've experimented with vLLM on prem for a couple workloads, but couldn't get inference stability at scale. TGI experiments had weird memory blowups. So we mostly rely on OpenAI in prod.
[01:06] Jordan: That's helpful — common story. A few things we'll want to validate: model compatibility (API parity), eval parity (does output match your current baseline), and throughput/latency on Dedicated. Also security: VPC, KMS, audit logs etc.
[01:18] Liam: On security — SOC2 is table stakes, but we also need KMS integration and VPC peering for private deployment. If private on-prem is an option that'd be great.
[01:26] Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC and customer KMS; our Private deployment gives a customer-managed control plane for on-prem/VPC. We'll share SOC2 artifacts and our security pack.
[01:34] Aisha: One thing we worry about: will prompts produce identical results? We have 200 regression prompts and a few finetuned-ish flows.
[01:40] Samir: For eval parity we can run your prompt set against the same open model variants in our Dedicated environment — we usually match models like Llama-2 derivatives or equivalent Open weights. If you have a finetune, we can host custom weights in Dedicated or do a connectivity approach.
[01:54] Carlos: How do you handle model variants? We're using a couple of OpenAI models — and a fallback to cheaper models during heavy load.
[02:02] Jordan: We provide a model catalog and routing policies — you can pin model versions, do canaries, and automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity is constrained. That helps with cost and reliability.
[02:12] Aisha: About vLLM/TGI compatibility — if we have an internal retried codepath that expects a vLLM behavior, will Redwood's runtime be noticeably different?
[02:20] Priya: Our runtime abstracts the common APIs; however, vLLM may have specific tokenization quirks or prompt templating differences. During the PoC we'll run parity tests — tokenization diff, output similarity metrics, and exact-match where necessary.
[02:34] Liam: Performance — can you hit our p95 / 700ms goal? We need to understand batch sizing and how it affects latency vs cost.
[02:42] Samir: Yes, this is central. Redwood's serving runtime uses continuous batching with latency SLO controls. For short prompts, we can configure smaller batch windows and dedicate capacity to meet p95 targets; we'll need to size GPU pools based on your RPS and sequence lengths. We'll propose an autoscale and burst plan in the benchmark.
[02:58] Carlos: Cost — what kind of delta should we expect migrating from OpenAI? Our current bill is significant but we need a concrete estimate.
[03:06] Jordan: We'll model unit economics in the pricing doc. Typically Dedicated reduces per-token costs for high-volume customers but adds a baseline commit. We'll run a cost comparison given your usage and target SLAs.
[03:16] Aisha: Embeddings — we use them heavily for search. Can you host vector stores or do we keep using our existing infra?
[03:22] Priya: Embeddings can be generated via Dedicated and you can choose to host vectors in your infra or use our managed embeddings storage. For compliance we often recommend hosting vectors yourself in your VPC.
[03:34] Carlos: Any concerns about prompt leakage or data residency?
[03:38] Jordan: With Dedicated/Private you control data at rest. We offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. There's also audit logs and retention controls. We'll share our compliance pack.
[03:46] Aisha: For PoC, we want to run two things: a 24-48h load test to measure p95/p99 and a regression test across our 200 prompts. Is that feasible?
[03:54] Priya: Absolutely. We'll need the prompt set, some representative payload sizes, and an API-keyed account to run the jobs. We'll also instrument traces to compare tokenization and outputs.
[04:06] Liam: Will you allow hooking into our telemetry? We want request/response traces shipped to our observability stack for a short period.
[04:12] Samir: We can do tracing hooks and per-route logs. For Dedicated we'll set up tracing integrations or provide trace exports. We'll work through retention and PII redaction.
[04:24] Jordan: Next, let's talk timeline — are you aiming to switch this quarter?
[04:28] Carlos: Ideally Q2 pilot and production late Q2 if PoC goes well. We have an investor demo in mid-May so timing is a bit firm.
[04:36] Jordan: Great — we can align a 2-4 week pilot starting mid-March if you provide prompts this week. We'll send pricing and PoC plan by Friday.
[04:44] Aisha: One more technical nuance — we sometimes use streaming tokens and function-calling; does Redwood support structured tool calling and streaming?
[04:52] Priya: Yes — streaming responses and function/tool calling are supported. We'll validate your exact tool schema during PoC.
[04:58] Carlos: Any limitations on quantized models? We plan to test q4_0 quantization to save memory on Dedicated.
[05:04] Samir: Our runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths and we can recommend profiles; sometimes there's small quality tradeoffs which we'll surface in the eval results.
[05:14] Jordan: Competitive question — you mentioned Anthropic and Azure earlier — any reasons you're not moving to their managed offerings?
[05:20] Carlos: Mainly cost and flexibility. Anthropic looked promising but contract terms and pricing were higher; Azure is more infra-heavy and we didn't want to manage the extra ops.
[05:30] Priya: Understood. For the PoC we'll include comparison metrics where feasible, but we usually benchmark against your current OpenAI baseline.
[05:36] Liam: For network — how much network config for VPC peering? Our security team is strict about CIDR whitelists and routes.
[05:42] Samir: We'll provide a network diagram and a minimal required ports doc; for Private deployments it's your control plane, so peering is straightforward. For Dedicated hosted we do VPC peering with strict egress controls.
[05:56] Carlos: Ok sounds good. Anything else we should know?
[06:00] Jordan: We'll email SOC2, security pack, and the pricing + PoC plan. Priya will follow up on the benchmark. Any final asks from your side?
[06:06] Aisha: Please include tokenization diffs in the eval and an example of how you surface regressions in Redwood Console.
[06:12] Priya: Will do — regression dashboards and alert hooks are part of our Optimize suite.
[06:18] Jordan: Great — we'll reconvene once the PoC details are in place. Thanks everyone.
[06:22] Carlos: Thanks — talk soon.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names transcribed as "Redwood Infer" or "Redwood dedik" in places; minor crosstalk and filler words.
